quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: For a first conviction of driving under the influence of alcohol, what could happen?

options.text: Lose your license for up to five years.
Be required to take a public education class on the dangers of drunk driving.
Be required to drive with a restricted occupational license.
Pay a fine of at least $300.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay a fine of at least $300.
questions.explanation: For a first offense of driving under the influence, you must pay a fine between $300 and $5,000. The exact amount depends on your blood alcohol concentration level.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, you should signal first, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do all of these things before you move to a new lane.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your vehicle will take longer to stop on slippery surfaces than on dry roads.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to slow down or stop unexpectedly?

options.text: Quickly tap your brake pedal a few times first.
Use your emergency brake.
Look over your shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Get ready to blow your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly tap your brake pedal a few times first.
questions.explanation: Tap your brake pedal three or four times quickly. This warns other drivers that you are slowing down when they may not expect it.

questions.question: What is the speed limit when yellow lights are flashing on a school zone speed limit sign?

options.text: 25 miles per hour
15 miles per hour
20 miles per hour
35 miles per hour

questions.explanation: When yellow lights on a school zone sign are flashing, or during marked school zone times, you must not drive faster than 15 miles per hour.

questions.question: What should you do if you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding.
Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one of the tracks is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks. Another train may be coming, even if there is only one track visible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It means you cannot continue driving in your current direction.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
No more or less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because it is harder to see. Other vehicles' headlights can blind you. Also, more tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Staying ahead of bad drivers by moving through traffic quickly.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to get around traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you notice dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you stay safe from aggressive, careless, tired, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a layer of water instead of gripping the road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase this risk. Speeding also makes hydroplaning more likely.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and flashing lights on. What must you do?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and sirens, you must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When leaving a driveway to enter the street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians can get out of your way.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know you are coming out.
Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians. Make your stop before crossing the sidewalk. You must do this by law.

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane road with no bike lanes and see a bicyclist ahead traveling in your direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down, wait until no traffic is coming, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist must get out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign before passing.
Honk your horn to warn the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait until no traffic is coming, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist the same way you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on normal roads or 5 feet on high-speed roads or when passing multiple bicyclists. Honking can startle riders and cause accidents.

questions.question: You are under 21 and are convicted of carrying a fake ID card. You will face a $500 fine and a 90-day license suspension:

options.text: Only if your blood alcohol level is 0.02 percent or higher.
Even if you were not driving.
Only if you were driving at the time.
Only if your blood alcohol level is 0.02 percent or higher and you were driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if you were not driving.
questions.explanation: If you are under 21 and convicted of carrying a fake ID, your license will be suspended even if you were not driving. The minimum penalties are a $500 fine, court costs, and a 90-day suspension for a first offense.

questions.question: Smoking while driving:

options.text: Does not affect your driving.
Helps keep you alert.
Is a distraction.
Is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: When passing a bicyclist, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn loudly to alert them.
Give them at least four feet of space.
Stay on the right side of your lane.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give them at least four feet of space.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to leave at least four feet of space between your vehicle and a bicyclist when passing.
